messages.subject: getAssociation with TSS
parts:
Hi , I did getAssociationWithTSS on an annotated object and I got the following which looks like

      target.row dist.to.feature feature.name feature.strand
322            1          359267    NM_172851              +
1119           2          247261    NR_102306              +
19             3          513215 NM_001160370              +
330            4            4615 NM_001012322              +
331            5         -125403    NR_038008              +
331.1          6          -87672    NR_038008              +


What is in the first column (322, 1119 etc)? Is this an identifier for the original differentially methylated base?

Thanks--Sumithra

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] getAssociation with TSS
parts:
you can ignore that, it is not a column actually just a row name and
it is a reminiscent of operations involving GenomicRanges.

The "target row" column contains the number of the row in the
methylKit object that is associated with the TSS. So target row column
is the identifier for the methylKit object that is annotated with TSS.

Best,
Altuna Akalin

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: getAssociation with TSS
parts:
there are no rows in that object, it is a list of multiple other data structures. But you can use getMembers() function to see if rows in the annotated bases/regions overlap with annotations(exon/intron/promoter) or not. This is slightly different from the output you will get from getAssociationWithTSS(), where row number of the annotated bases/regions are kept as a separate column. 

Whereas getMembers() output has the same length and order of rows as the annotated base/regions.

Best,
Altuna

You may safely ignore the first column!
